name: SP Lead Insights for Contact Form 7
author: salmanpatnee

sections.description:
Here’s the thing nobody talks about with Contact Form 7: it’s great at sending emails, but it tells you nothing about what happens before and after.

Someone visits your page, sees your form, and leaves without submitting. You’ll never know. Someone submits a fake email from a disposable address just to download your lead magnet. It hits your inbox looking like a real lead. Your contact form on a page you spent weeks optimizing has a 3% conversion rate — and you have no idea.

That’s not a Contact Form 7 problem. CF7 does exactly what it says. But if you’re using forms to grow your business, you need more than “message sent.”

That’s why I built SP Lead Insights.

What it actually does

You get a real dashboard. Every CF7 form on your site shows up with its view count, submission count, and conversion rate. You don’t have to set up Google Analytics goals, install tag manager snippets, or learn a new tool. It’s just there, in your WordPress admin, the day you install it.

You can see every submission. A searchable, sortable log of every form entry — date, form name, whether it was delivered. When a client emails you saying they filled out your form three days ago and never heard back, you can pull up the log and know in ten seconds what actually happened.

Spam gets stopped before it reaches you. You can build an email domain blocklist — just type in a domain like mailinator.com and hit Add. Anyone who tries to submit a form with that domain gets a validation error. They never get through. The Blocked log shows you everything that was stopped and why.

A honeypot catches bots automatically. No setup. It’s just on.

Your data stays on your server

No accounts to create. No API keys. No data leaving your WordPress install. SP Lead Insights doesn’t phone home, doesn’t connect to any third-party service, and doesn’t store anything it doesn’t need.

What it does store: which form, what type of event, whether it was delivered, and a one-way hash of the IP address. Not the email address. Not the name. Not what anyone typed into your form. Ever.

The IP hashing uses HMAC-SHA256 with your site’s own AUTH_SALT as the key — meaning the hash is unique to your site and can’t be reversed. That’s the GDPR-safe approach, and it’s baked into how the plugin works, not an option you have to remember to turn on.

Good fit for

  • Freelancers and agencies who need to show clients whether their forms are working
  • Small business owners running their own site and wondering why leads seem slow
  • Marketers who want conversion data without setting up a full analytics stack
  • Anyone who’s ever gotten a spam submission and thought “there has to be a better way”

Everything included

Analytics
* Automatic view and submission tracking on every CF7 form — no per-form setup
* Conversion rate per form (views ÷ submissions), calculated for you
* 30-day breakdown in the Analytics tab
* Dashboard widget showing your top 5 forms at a glance, updated daily

Submission Log
* Every form entry in one place: date, form name, delivery status
* Sortable columns so you can find what you’re looking for quickly

Spam Filtering
* Email Domain Blocklist — one domain per line, blocks the whole domain
* Blocked submissions get a real CF7 validation error, not a silent drop
* Blocked Attempts log with timestamp, form name, and reason
* Honeypot field injected automatically into every form

Privacy
* No raw IPs stored — HMAC-SHA256 hash only, keyed to your AUTH_SALT
* No field values, no email addresses, no names — ever
* Zero outbound HTTP requests
* Works with the WordPress privacy tools out of the box
sections.installation:
1. Upload the sp-lead-insights-for-contact-form-7 folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it under Plugins > Installed Plugins.
  3. Make sure Contact Form 7 is active too.

That’s it — tracking starts immediately, no configuration needed.

To block spam domains, go to SP Lead Insights > Settings and add them to the Email Domain Blocklist.
sections.faq:
Does this store what people type into my forms?

No — never. SP Lead Insights only records that a submission happened, which form it came from, whether it was delivered, and a hashed IP address. The actual content of the submission is never touched.

Is this GDPR-compliant?

Yes. IP addresses are stored as one-way HMAC-SHA256 hashes using your site’s AUTH_SALT as the secret key. The hash can’t be reversed, and raw IPs are never written to the database.

One thing worth knowing: because we store hashed IPs rather than email addresses, the standard WordPress privacy erasure tool can’t look up records by email. If you receive a Subject Access Request, the data tied to that person is the hashed IP — which is already anonymised and can’t be linked back to anyone without the original IP address.

Will it slow down my site?

No. View tracking uses a small JavaScript beacon that fires after the page loads — it doesn’t block anything. The backend endpoint it hits is lightweight. You won’t notice it.

Does it work if I’m using a caching plugin?

Yes. Because view tracking happens client-side (in the browser), it works even when the page is served from cache and PHP never runs. That’s by design.

Can I block those disposable/throwaway email services?

Yes, that’s exactly what the blocklist is for. Add mailinator.com, guerrillamail.com, or any other domain you want to block. Submissions from those domains will fail with a validation error before the form sends.

Does it automatically track all my forms?

Yes. Every active CF7 form on your site is tracked from the moment you activate the plugin. You don’t need to configure anything per form.

screenshots.caption: Dashboard widget — top converting forms at a glance, with conversion rate, views, and submissions for the last 7 days.
Analytics tab — per-form breakdown of views, submissions, and conversion rate over the last 30 days.
Submissions log — searchable, sortable list of every form entry with date, form name, and delivery status.
Blocked tab — log of spam attempts stopped by the domain blocklist, with reason and source.
Settings — Email Domain Blocklist; add domains one at a time to permanently reject their submissions with a validation error.
